claim: Hist2h2be (H2be) is a replication-independent histone variant expressed exclusively by olfactory chemosensory neurons.
source_text: We have identified a replication-independent histone variant, Hist2h2be (referred to herein as H2be ), which is expressed exclusively by olfactory chemosensory neurons.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental observations including ISH analyses showing H2be expression limited to MOE and VNO sensory neurons (Figure 1A-D), and molecular characterization showing poly-A tail and long 3'-UTR consistent with replication-independent expression.

claim: H2BE levels are heterogeneous among olfactory neurons but stereotyped according to the identity of the co-expressed olfactory receptor (OR).
source_text: Levels of H2BE are heterogeneous among olfactory neurons, but stereotyped according to the identity of the co-expressed olfactory receptor (OR).
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through quantitative fluorescence microscopy showing that each of 42 tested ORs is consistently associated with a stereotyped level of H2BE, with 73% showing significantly less variation within OR type than across the entire neuronal population (Figure 2F,G).

claim: Changes in H2be expression affect olfactory function and OR representation in the adult olfactory epithelium.
source_text: Gain- and loss-of-function experiments demonstrate that changes in H2be expression affect olfactory function and OR representation in the adult olfactory epithelium.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by behavioral testing showing H2be-KO mice learn odor discrimination tasks more slowly (Figure 3D), and by microarray and FISH analyses showing altered OR expression frequencies in both H2be-KO and H2be-GF mice (Figures 4, 5).

claim: H2BE expression is reduced by sensory activity.
source_text: We show that H2BE expression is reduced by sensory activity
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through unilateral naris occlusion experiments showing dramatically higher H2BE on the closed side (Figure 8A,B), and odor exposure experiments showing reduced H2BE levels in neurons expressing ORs stimulated by specific ligands (Figure 8D-F).

claim: H2BE promotes neuronal cell death such that inactive olfactory neurons display higher levels of H2BE and shorter life spans.
source_text: it promotes neuronal cell death, such that inactive olfactory neurons display higher levels of the variant and shorter life spans.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by apoptosis analyses showing 45% lower apoptosis frequency in H2be-KO mice (Figure 7C) and twofold higher apoptosis in H2be-GF mice (Figure 7E), along with BrdU labeling showing increased neuronal survival in H2be-KO and decreased survival in H2be-GF mice (Figure 7D,F).

claim: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) of H2BE differ from those of canonical H2B.
source_text: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) of H2BE differ from those of the canonical H2B, consistent with a role for H2BE in altering transcription.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through immunofluorescence showing inverse correlation between H2BE and H2B-Lys5-Me levels (Figure 14A,B), ELISA confirming antibody reactivity (Figure 14C), and western blot showing no detectable Lys5-Me modification on FLAG-H2BE (Figure 14F).

evidence_reasoning: Inferred from multiple lines of evidence including activity-dependent H2BE regulation, effects on neuronal longevity, and changes in OR representation following environmental manipulation (UNO and odor exposure experiments).
